30.x: “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man..”: The context suggests that the “sign” is the unmistakable breakthrough of Jesus Himself. The universe-wide lightning flash of His arrival is the sign that vindicates His Word. “..and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn..”: This is a direct quote from Zechariah 12:10-12. The mourning here is not a holy, repentant sorrow leading to salvation; it is the absolute terror and panic (“men’s hearts failing them for fear”) of a rebellious world that suddenly realizes the God they mocked, denied, and persecuted is real, and He has arrived to execute judgement. “..and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven..”: Jesus intentionally utilizes the language of Daniel 7:13-14. In the OT, riding on the clouds is a visual action reserved exclusively for YHWH (Ps 104:3). By executing this action, Jesus claims to be the same YHWH as in the OT.

The glory of the Father and the glory of the Son are not two separate, competing lights. Jesus is the “brightness of His glory, and the express image of His person” (Heb 1:3 KJV). The Father is the invisible, infinite fountain of Spirit; the Son is the visible, physical face of that exact same Spirit. When Jesus descends in Mt 24:30, he does not shine with a secondary, borrowed light. He shines with the Glory of the Father because the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily inside of him (Col 2:9). The very light that blinds the rebellious nations in the raw, unveiled glory of the one true God, breaking through the physical body of Jesus Christ to claim His inheritance over the earth.
